clue.text: Quiet church out East is run-down

parts.note: the hushing sound asking for quiet

indicators.note: with a letter put out, it is dropped from the word it sat in

parts.note: an abbey is a monastic church
E is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A quiet church in the east of town has fallen into disrepair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out East' reads as a location in the surface, but it tells you to drop the compass letter from the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shabby is worn, neglected and dilapidated, just as a run-down building looks.

clue.text: Genuine playing area raised in function

indicators.note: one thing sits inside the other, so the function wraps the playing area

parts.note: the sine is a trigonometric function

indicators.note: in a down clue something raised is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public playing field

explanation.surface: A genuine sports ground is built up for a public event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' suggests a social event, but it is the mathematical sense; a rec is a British recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere feelings are honestly held and not pretended, which is what genuine ones are.

clue.text: Politician protected by first-class defence

indicators.note: something protected by another is surrounded by it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: A1 means first-class; the digit stands in as the letter I
Lib is short for a Liberal

explanation.surface: A politician hides behind a top-quality legal defence.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written with the figure 1 read as the letter I, and LIB goes between the A and the I.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is the plea that the accused was elsewhere when the crime happened, a defence used in court.

clue.text: Refuse to steal a ship before first escaping

parts.note: to bag is slang for stealing
taken as written
SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: first asks only for the opening letter of the word it qualifies

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone declines to hijack a vessel before getting away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning waste. 'Before' places the earlier pieces ahead of the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagasse is the fibrous waste left after sugar cane is crushed, so it is refuse in the rubbish sense.

clue.text: Excellent fruit year

parts.note: a soft stone fruit
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A vintage year for fruit is described as excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Peachy is informal praise meaning fine or splendid, as in everything being peachy.

clue.text: Chicory is strangely veined

indicators.note: something arranged strangely is out of its usual order, so the letters move

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A salad leaf is noted for its odd pattern of veins.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a leafy salad plant of the chicory family; in Britain the names are used for one another.

clue.text: An examination involving several questions

parts.note: surface reading: a school or university test paper
setter's reading: a religious instruction drilled as fixed questions and answers

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like an ordinary exam; the questions are the set ones of religious teaching, learnt with their set replies.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechism is a summary of Christian doctrine taught as a series of questions with prescribed answers.

clue.text: A river in eg New Zealand — Tay, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters are only a possible arrangement, one to be reworked

parts.note: taken as written
NZ is the country's abbreviation
taken as written; the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: A quiz-style question asks whether a river in New Zealand could be the Tay.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is a red herring river; its letters, with EG and NZ, make the Chinese one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yangtze is the longest river in China and in Asia.

clue.text: In which a number of months are accounted for

definitions.text: In which a number of months are accounted for

parts.words: In which a number of months are accounted for
parts.note: surface reading: a stretch of time in which some months are simply counted up
setter's reading: the twelve months over which the books are made up and taxes reckoned

explanation.walkthrough: 'Accounted for' sounds like simply counted; it is the bookkeeping sense, accounts drawn up for a period.
explanation.definitionFit: A financial year is the twelve-month period for which an organisation prepares its accounts or a government its budget.

clue.text: Opposing article backing Information Technology

parts.note: the indefinite article

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the abbreviation is read from its end

parts.note: the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece supports computing while seemingly standing against it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' sounds like supporting, which pulls against 'Opposing'; here it means reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as a preposition or adjective means against or hostile to something.

clue.text: At work, hooter is kept to it

definitions.text: At work, hooter is kept to it

parts.words: At work, hooter is kept to it
parts.note: surface reading: a factory hooter sounding at the workplace
setter's reading: slang for the nose, held to a sharpening wheel in the idiom for working hard

explanation.walkthrough: A hooter suggests a factory siren; it is slang for the nose, as in keeping one's nose to the stone that grinds.
explanation.definitionFit: A grindstone is a revolving stone for sharpening, and the idiom about the nose means toiling steadily.

clue.text: One in opposition with advice saved lot in trouble

indicators.note: things in trouble are thrown into disorder, so these letters get jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rescued group in difficulty gets guidance from someone who disagrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A devil's advocate takes the contrary side of an argument deliberately to test it.

clue.text: See 11
The awareness of one sitting in judgement

indicators.note: someone sitting in a place is inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a court's judgement on punishment
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A judge sitting on the bench shows awareness of the case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sitting in judgement' reads as a judge at work; I goes inside SENTENCE, after its first T.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel and perceive, a basic consciousness of the world.

clue.text: Could be applied to "The Twist"

parts.note: surface reading: a label for the 1960s dance or a novel's hero
setter's reading: an adjective describing twisting force as in engineering

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest the dance or Oliver Twist; it is simply the adjective for twisting.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsion is the twisting of an object by opposing forces, so torsional describes anything relating to a twist.

clue.text: Light sack

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ignite or set alight
second meaning: to dismiss from a job

explanation.surface: A bag that weighs little.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to set burning and to dismiss someone from employment.

clue.text: Company: one with branches at beginning of millennium

parts.note: a fir is a tree, which has branches

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A company with branch offices opened as the new millennium began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branches' suggests the company's offices, but the one with branches is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm is a business concern, another word for a commercial company.

clue.text: Bold footballer

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an attacking player in a team

explanation.surface: A daring player on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for brazen or pushy behaviour and a noun for an attacking position in football.

clue.text: I'm top name in performance at Christmas

indicators.note: the letters go in, that is into, the form of the show, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A star boasts of top billing in the festive show.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is slight: 'in' turns the first three words into the show's name. Pantomime is a British family stage show staged around Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a comic family theatre show with songs and slapstick, traditionally staged in Britain over the Christmas season.

clue.text: Engaged in fight against time on American vehicle

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
the usual abbreviation
a sled is a sledge

explanation.surface: Someone battled the clock while riding an American car.
explanation.definitionFit: To have tussled is to have struggled or scuffled with someone, a past-tense verb for fighting.

clue.text: Traffic light set up to indicate bend

parts.note: to mean is to signify or indicate

indicators.note: in a down clue something set up stands upside down, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: the stop light

explanation.surface: Traffic lights are put up to warn drivers of a curve ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A meander is a winding curve in a river or road, which is a bend.

clue.text: This attracts good artist around

indicators.note: around says the artist is placed about the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: Édouard Manet, the French painter
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Good art draws people in.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist is the French Impressionist painter, a regular crossword source for these letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet is an object that pulls iron towards it, so it is the thing that attracts.

clue.text: Common-or-garden salt

parts.note: surface reading: plain table salt from the kitchen
setter's reading: an old salt is a sailor, here one of the lowest rank

explanation.walkthrough: Salt looks like the seasoning; an old salt is a sailor, and the plain one is the navy's lowest grade.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the most junior rating in the Royal Navy, an unremarkable sailor at the bottom of the ranks.

clue.text: See 21
The sailor's a short distance nearer the stern

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
taken as written
ft, the abbreviation for feet, a short measure

explanation.surface: A sailor stands just a little way towards the back of the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sailor's' reads as possessive; the 's is just 'is', joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaft is a nautical term for behind or towards the rear part of a vessel.

clue.text: It was shot as part of history

definitions.text: It was shot as part of history

parts.words: It was shot as part of history
parts.note: surface reading: footage filmed for a historical documentary
setter's reading: an iron ball fired from old artillery, now a thing of the past

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests filming; the thing was literally fired, and has passed into history.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannonball is the solid iron projectile fired from a cannon in earlier centuries of warfare.

clue.text: Confidential assistant gives help with start of education

parts.note: aid is help

indicators.note: the start of a word is only its first letter

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A trusted assistant helps a pupil get started at school.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a personal assistant to an important person, often trusted with private matters.

clue.text: Expand on obscure detail

indicators.note: something obscure is muddled and unclear, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to say more about a little-known point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expand on' looks like one phrase meaning elaborate; the definition is 'Expand' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilate is to widen or enlarge, and also to speak at length, both senses of expanding.

clue.text: The lender losing credit is the one to check

indicators.note: a word losing something has those letters taken out of it

parts.note: one to whom money is owed
CR is the bookkeeping abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A lender whose credit dries up has to be kept in check.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor reviews and corrects text before publication, so checking copy is the job.
